results_sub: Same model (Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite), two agent designs, 6 companies, 18 forks per cell

variant_names.misinfo: False claim in a search result
variant_names.poison: Hidden instruction in a search result

results_notes: False claim: brief_py repeated it in 15 of 18 forks, brief_ts in 3 of 18. Hidden instruction: 13 of 18 vs 0 of 18.
Both agents read the planted text in 18 of 18 forks, so the gap comes from agent design. Per company: brief_py worse at 6 of 6 companies (sign test p = 0.031).
Per run: exact McNemar p = 0.0005 and 0.0002. Both agents recovered from every provider outage.
fork_notes: Replay: 12 runs, 0 misses, $0.168 to $0, 6.0x faster including agent start-up.

Position matters: the same false claim at brief_py's last search (earlier searches replayed byte for byte) was repeated in 1 of 12 forks, against 15 of 18 at the first search. Lower at all 6 companies.
A fork only pays for the steps after the change: 42% cheaper than a fresh run at the first search, 96% at the last.
engineering: Runs on a stock Bifrost v2.5.1 build; uses only public plugin hooks (HTTPTransportPreHook / PostHook) plus Relays, virtual keys and provider retries.
36 Go tests (race detector on) cover fingerprinting, diffs, the store, every mode and mutation through the real hooks, and the run API. 22 Python tests for scoring and statistics. CI on every push.
Overhead: about 15 µs to fingerprint a request; about 0.36 ms per replayed step including the atomic cassette write.
Agents in two languages needed no Rewind code: a base URL and one header.
Opened upstream as maximhq/bifrost issue #10047 and pull request #10048.
limits: Only traffic through the gateway is recorded; local files or clocks aren't.
Streams are recorded but not replayed as streams yet.
Both agents were written for this project; six companies; forks at the first search.
